If you're not in a rush to get your hands on the latest Apple product on launch day, and you don't mind waiting a bit, Apple's official certified refurbished product store has always been a reliable choice. Generally speaking, about three months after a new product goes on sale, the first batch of refurbished units will appear on the Apple website.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but be aware that the standards and warranty terms they use are different……

Apple Certified Refurbished Products

Buying from the Apple Certified Refurbished Products store typically saves you around 15%, and the products are identical to brand-new units. Specifically, Apple promises all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing performed by Apple
  • Brand-new housing, so absolutely no scratches or wear
  • Brand-new battery, so battery life is the same as a new unit
  • Comes with all original accessories and cables
  • Covered by Apple's standard one-year warranty, with the same coverage as a new unit
  • You can also purchase AppleCare+ additionally

Basically the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box instead of the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed is usually priced more competitively, but note that the product condition does not come with the same guarantees:

  • Inspected and tested by the seller, not Apple
  • Used housing, so there will be scratches and wear (see below)
  • Used battery, only guaranteed to still have at least 80% of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be genuine Apple products
  • Comes with a 90-day Amazon warranty instead of Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding scratches and wear, Amazon offers three quality grades:

  • Premium / Excellent: no wear visible when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: minor scratches when viewed from 12 inches away, barely noticeable to the naked eye
  • Acceptable: scratches easily visible and palpable

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is even vaguer than Amazon, and doesn't clearly state what you're getting for your money:

  • No commitment whatsoever on cosmetic condition, only claiming "performance and reliability like new"
  • No specific information on battery condition, only what's mentioned above
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium grade comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair grades only get 90 days. The company does not clearly define what each grade actually represents.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want a product that looks identical to new and comes with an Apple warranty, the Apple Refurbished Store is clearly the top choice.

However, Amazon Renewed pricing can indeed be a lot cheaper, so if you're willing to accept the trade-offs listed above, it's still a pretty good deal. Especially if you'll listen to us and save some money to upgrade to the iPhone 17 Pro instead of this year's new model (you're only missing one feature), there are some genuinely attractive deals here:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (original price $1,599) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (original price $1,599) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (original price $1,599) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (original price $1,299) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (original price $1,299) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (original price $1,299) — only $1 more than the all-time low

As for Walmart Restored, their promises are really too vague for me to say with any confidence, but if you're not satisfied, you can always opt to return it.
